extracted.intended_audience: university technology transfer professionals, IP counsel, research administrators, and practitioners dealing with export controls and international IP obligations
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes international (WTO/TRIPs) minimum standards for intellectual property rights and related guidance on U.S. export controls and embargoes as they affect technology transfers and university research. Useful for university tech transfer offices, counsel, and researchers evaluating compliance and contract language.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Department controls on defense articles and technical data
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Department regulates the sending or taking of a defense article out of the U.S. or disclosing technical data to a foreign person whether in the U.S. or abroad. 22 C.F.R. § 120.17(1), (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the ITAR regime: disclosures to foreign persons (deemed exports) and physical exports of defense articles are regulated. Treat disclosures of controlled technical data and transfers of defense articles as requiring review for ITAR coverage and potential licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce Department controls on exports and technology release (EAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commerce Department regulates actual shipments out of the U.S. as well as a release of technology or source code subject to the controls to in a foreign country or to a foreign national in the United States. 15 C.F.R. § 734.2(b)(1)-(2) (2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the EAR, exporting or releasing controlled technology/source code to foreign nationals (including deemed exports) or transferring abroad can trigger licensing requirements. Evaluate ECCN and export licensing obligations under EAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental research exclusion may be limited or invalidated
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of certain restrictions (e.g., publication or foreign national restrictions imposed by sponsors) or adherence to government-imposed national security controls can invalidate the fundamental research exclusion under ITAR (22 C.F.R. § 120.11(8)) and EAR (15 C.F.R. § 734.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a research award imposes publication/foreign-national restrictions or national-security clauses, institutions may lose the fundamental research exclusion and become subject to export controls; licensing or other controls may then apply. Under EAR there is a limited licensing exemption when specific government national-security controls are imposed and fully adhered to; if controls are not satisfied, licensing requirements apply and violations may result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited 'fundamental research' exception for certain allied-country research access
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited exception relates to an expanded 'fundamental research' exclusion involving research satellites and related information exports to government research institutions and to universities in European Union countries, NATO countries, major non-NATO allies, and European Space Agency countries where only nationals of these countries will have access. See 22 C.F.R. 121.1 XV(a) or (e), 123.16(b)(10)(equipment), and 125.4(d)(services/information/instruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow exception permits certain controlled transfers where access is limited to nationals of specified allied countries; verify nationality limits and specific regulatory citations carefully before relying on this exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use controlled sponsor proprietary information at sponsor's site when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: It is best to use controlled sponsor proprietary information only at the sponsor’s site if possible. This places the primary burden for securing the information from unlicensed disclosure to foreign nationals on the sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If faculty or staff access controlled information at the sponsor's site, they must secure notes and avoid disclosure to foreign nationals. If the university accepts such information on campus, implement appropriate security measures to prevent unauthorized deemed exports in the U.S. or exports abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of accepting sponsor-imposed restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of publication or foreign-national restrictions in research awards means export controls apply to research; foreigners cannot participate or an export or deemed export license must be obtained and/or other requirements satisfied, and security measures must be implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions accepting these restrictions accept fundamental changes to campus openness and nationality-blind policies; options include negotiation, declining funding, or implementing licensing/security measures—be aware negotiations can delay research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public domain/publicly available information definitions and websites as publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in the 'public domain' and 'publicly available' is outlined in ITAR under 22 C.F.R. § 120.11 and § 120.10(5). Information in the 'public domain' and 'publicly available' is outlined in EAR under 15 C.F.R. § 734.3(b)(3) and §§ 734.7-734.9. Web sites are clearly an authorized means of publication under EAR and are probably an acceptable means of publication under ITAR, although there is no formal guidance from the Department of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication on a public website generally places information in the public domain for EAR purposes—this can affect whether export controls apply. For patent filings, check specific rules on export controls of patent applications (22 C.F.R. § 125.2(b); 15 C.F.R. § 734.10; 37 C.F.R. § 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clause requiring compliance with U.S. export laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical contractual provision: parties acknowledge they are subject to U.S. laws controlling export of technology/items and/or restricting transactions with sanctioned countries/individuals; transfers may require licenses or written assurances, and securing such license cannot be guaranteed; parties must request and obtain written agreement before providing restricted Technology and Items and must explicitly acknowledge application of such Restrictions in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include express export-control compliance clauses in agreements, require written acknowledgements, designate points of contact for notices, and preserve ability to withhold transfer until licenses/assurances obtained. Expect that license approval is not guaranteed; plan contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFAC/embargo and sanctions compliance (IEEPA/TWEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Export/transaction restrictions and embargoes may be imposed under statutes such as IEEPA and the Trading with the Enemy Act, and administered by OFAC. Recent changes include revised general licenses codified at 31 CFR 515.577 (Cuba), 31 CFR 538.529 (Sudan), and 31 CFR 560.538 (Iran).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check OFAC lists, general licenses, and current press releases/actions before engaging in transfers, collaborations, or transactions involving sanctioned countries or parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: obligation to comply with Paris Convention Articles and principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 1 of TRIPs requires that members comply with Articles 1, 2, and 19 of the Paris Convention and adopts the national treatment requirement and adds a most-favored nation provision requiring member countries to treat nationals of all WTO-member states no less favorably than their own nationals or nationals of any other country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRIPs imposes minimum international obligations; national IP laws must meet TRIPs minimums including national treatment and MFN. TRIPs does not require Paris Convention membership but requires compliance with those Articles' principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: copyright protection minimums (Berne compliance and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: An obligation to comply with the provisions of Articles 1–21 and the appendix to the Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works, coupled with an express statement that 'copyright protection shall extend to expressions and not to ideas, procedures, methods of operation, or mathematical concepts as such.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Member states must align copyright law with Berne standards; protect expressions but not underlying ideas or methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: computer programs and database protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement to treat computer programs, whether in source code or object code, as literary works for copyright protection purposes and to provide protection for databases if their selection or arrangement 'constitute intellectual creations' without prejudice to any copyright subsisting in the data or material itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure domestic law treats software as copyrightable literary works and provides sui generis or copyright protection for databases where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: rental rights and related protections
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement to give to authors of computer programs and cinematographic works and producers of phonograms the rights in certain circumstances to control commercial rental of the originals or copies of their works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider rental/right-of-lending regimes in national law to comply with TRIPs obligations for these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: minimum copyright duration
rubrics_metrics.description: An obligation that, in respect of works other than photographs and works of applied art, the normal duration of copyright protection shall be at least fifty years from the death of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic durations shorter than 50 years post mortem are inconsistent with TRIPs; update national statutes accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: limit fair-use/exceptions to certain special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: An obligation to limit fair-use provisions and similar conditions on the exercise of copyright to 'certain special cases which do not conflict with normal exploitation of a work and do not unreasonably prejudice the legitimate interests of the right holder.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design limitations and exceptions narrowly so they do not conflict with normal exploitation and do not unreasonably prejudice rights holders' legitimate interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: performers, phonogram producers and broadcasters protections and durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations to afford certain minimum rights for protection of performers, producers of phonograms, and broadcasting organizations. Performers: protection against fixation of unfixed works, reproduction of fixation, and unauthorized broadcasting for at least fifty years. Phonogram producers: protection against reproduction for at least fifty years from fixation. Broadcasters: rights to control fixation or rebroadcasting for at least twenty years from broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure national laws provide the specified protections and durations subject to permitted conditions and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: trademark registrability and distinctiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Any visually perceptible sign (including letters, numerals, and colors) capable of distinguishing goods or services shall be regarded as capable of functioning as a trademark and registerable; member states may refuse registration for signs that lack inherent distinctiveness unless they have acquired distinctiveness through use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a broad registrability standard but allow refusal of inherently non-distinctive signs unless distinctiveness acquired by use.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: registration/use relationship and nonuse timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration may be conditioned on the mark being used. However, actual use must not be a prerequisite for filing an application for registration. Nor shall an application be refused simply because an intended use has not commenced within three years of the application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow filing without prior use; do not deny registration solely because use has not started within three years of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: protection of well-known marks extends to services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paris Convention provisions relating to protection of well-known marks must apply to marks used in respect of services as well as goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend protections for well-known marks in national law to cover services as well as goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: trademark limitations must consider legitimate interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations on the rights conferred by trademark protection, such as fair use of descriptive terms, must take account of the legitimate interests of the trademark owner and third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance exceptions and limitations to avoid unduly prejudicing trademark owners while preserving legitimate third-party uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: nonuse cancellation and acceptable excuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries that provide for cancellation of registrations on the ground of nonuse must allow a period of nonuse of at least three years without a valid reason for the nonuse before such provisions may be invoked. Excuses outside the owner’s control (e.g., import restrictions) are valid reasons; third-party use under owner control benefits the owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement nonuse cancellation procedures with at least a three-year grace period and recognize legitimate excuses for nonuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: encumbrances and compulsory licensing of trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Encumbrances on the use of a trademark (such as requirements that its use must be linked with some other mark) are barred. Although countries may impose conditions on licensing, compulsory licensing of trademarks is banned and prohibitions on assignment without transfer of the business are banned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit encumbrances that unduly restrict trademark use; do not allow compulsory licensing of trademarks or forced assignment divorced from business transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: geographical indications — prevent misleading origin claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Member territories must make provision for interested parties to prevent use of a designation that falsely indicates the geographical origin of goods if this misleads the public and to prevent or cancel registration of a trademark with a similar effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide legal remedies to prevent false or misleading geographical indications; consider additional protections for wines and spirits.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: geographical indications — wines and spirits multilateral system
rubrics_metrics.description: More specific provisions were agreed for wines and spirits, calling for establishment of a multilateral system for notification and registration of geographical indications for wines and further negotiations for increased protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement notification/registration mechanisms for wines/spirits and follow TRIPs multilateral system developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: industrial design protection minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles 25 and 26 require member territories to provide protection for new and original independently created industrial designs for a period of at least ten years. No need to protect a design dictated essentially by technical or functional considerations. Protection must guard against articles embodying a copy or substantial copy and may be by industrial design law or copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure design protection covers new/original designs for ≥10 years and exempts purely functional designs; allow protection by design law or copyright where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: nondiscrimination in patent availability and enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents shall be available and enjoyable without discrimination as to the place of invention, the field of technology, and whether the product is imported or produced locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend domestic laws (e.g., 35 U.S.C. changes) to avoid discrimination against inventions by origin, technology field, or production method.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: permissible exclusions from patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: The only types of inventions that countries can exclude from patentability are: (a) those whose exploitation would prejudice public order or morality; (b) those involving diagnostic, therapeutic, or surgical methods for the treatment of humans or animals; (c) plants and animals; or (d) essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals. Countries excluding plants must provide some alternative means of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit exclusions narrowly to these categories and ensure alternative protection for plant-related subject matter if patents are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: limitations/exceptions to patent rights (Article 30 standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries may allow limited exceptions (e.g., experimental-use or personal-use rights) provided such rights 'must not unreasonably conflict with a normal exploitation of a patent and do not unreasonably prejudice the legitimate interests of the patent owner, taking account the legitimate interests of third parties.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design exceptions narrowly so they do not unreasonably harm patent exploitation or owners' legitimate interests; consider third-party needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPs: compulsory licensing procedural and substantive constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licenses or other 'official licenses' are only to be permitted after consideration of the individual situation. Any such license shall be nonexclusive and assignable only with the business that enjoys its use and, except in cases of national emergency, the requester must have made efforts to obtain a voluntary license on reasonable commercial terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement compulsory licensing regimes with safeguards: case-by-case consideration, nonexclusive character, assignment limits tied to business transfer, and prior good-faith efforts to obtain voluntary licenses unless emergency/other exceptions apply.
